rationale.consistency: Matches codebase conventions, naming, and style perfectly; cleanly integrates with existing functions and variables.
rationale.edge_cases: Handles decoding and case-insensitivity well, though backwards byte-by-byte parsing allows rare constructed escapes (like %252F) to piecemeal match a literal escape (%2F).
rationale.scope: Exactly fulfills the requirements, replacing the flawed reverse() approach with a bespoke backward-stepping algorithm with no unrelated changes.
rationale.readability: Clear structure with excellent comments explaining the constraints, algorithmic choices, and the failure of the naive reverse approach.
rationale.robustness: Safe bounds checking, graceful handling of url.PathUnescape errors, and safe against out-of-bounds panics on mismatched string lengths.
rationale.maintainability: Self-contained and logical, though the backward byte-by-byte traversal introduces subtle asymmetry compared to standard forward parsing.
